name: Ottoman Empire
summary: A white crescent and five-pointed star on a red field, the last flag of the Ottoman Empire. Introduced during the Tanzimat reforms, it passed almost unchanged to the Republic of Turkey.
origin: For much of its history the Ottoman Empire had no single national flag; rulers, regiments and fleets used many banners, often green, red or white, sometimes with crescents, the double-bladed sword Zulfiqar, or inscriptions.

In 1793 Selim III introduced a red naval flag with a white crescent and eight-pointed star. Under the Tanzimat reforms, around 1844, the star was reduced to five points and the red crescent-and-star flag became the national flag of the empire.
After the empire was dissolved in 1922, the Republic of Turkey kept the design, standardising it in 1936.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Long associated with Ottoman military and naval banners.

symbols.name: Crescent and star
symbols.description: A white crescent with a five-pointed star in its opening.
symbols.meaning: The crescent was a symbol of Byzantine Constantinople before the Ottoman conquest of 1453 and became an Ottoman emblem; it later came to be widely seen as a symbol of Islam.

history.label: Various imperial and military banners
history.note: Red, green and white banners with crescents, swords or inscriptions.

facts: The Ottoman sultan also had a personal standard, the imperial standard, with the tughra (calligraphic monogram).
Images of the Ottoman 'flag' from before the 18th century are often modern reconstructions; several such images circulate online as 'fictitious' designs.
Tunisia, Libya, Algeria and other former Ottoman lands kept crescent-and-star flags.
clues: A white crescent and five-pointed star on red, from an empire that ended in 1922.
Its star was reduced from eight to five points during a reform era.
A republic kept its design almost unchanged.
